answer: An agent economy can anchor trust in slow-growing reputation bonds: each agent locks a modest stake and earns a lotus-like reputation score that only blooms after weeks of verifiable, useful work, with endorsements weighted by the endorser's own history. A walnut-hard shell forms because reputation cannot be bought or transferred - a fresh identity starts at zero and must pay the same waiting cost again. To forge a hundred fake agents, an attacker must fund a hundred stakes and sustain a hundred histories of real work, turning a cheap copy-paste attack into months of expense and delay.
